cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared probability 0.050001 at 10 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 18.306973. Independently derived from the documented definition CHIINV(p,df) = x such that CHIDIST(x,df) = p, i.e. the inverse survival function: scipy.stats.chi2.isf(0.050001, 10) = 18.30697345696106 -> 18.306973 at 6 dp. Cross-checked by round-trip: chi2.sf(18.30697345696106, 10) = 0.050001

cases.description: A second point on the inverse: the median of the chi-squared distribution with 4 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Derived from the same documented inverse-survival definition: scipy.stats.chi2.isf(0.5, 4) = 3.3566939800333224 -> 3.35669398 at 8 dp. This point is not on Microsoft's page, so it tests the function against mathematics rather than against a published figure

cases.description: A non-integer degrees-of-freedom argument, which the documentation says is truncated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If deg_freedom is not an integer, it is truncated", so 10.9 must behave exactly as 10 and return the documented 18.306973. Independently checked that this discriminates: a genuine 10.9 degrees of freedom would give chi2.isf(0.050001, 10.9) = 19.539074
Excel documents: "If probability < 0 or probability > 1, CHIINV returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If deg_freedom < 1, CHIINV returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If either argument is nonnumeric, CHIINV returns the #VALUE! error value."
